guards.what: G1: Sign-aware power typing missing from Artifact interception (PowerCmd.apply's Artifact check uses the static power_cls.power_type class attribute instead of C#'s GetTypeForAmount(amount))
guards.issue: MECHANISM (confirmed): cmds.py:299 checks `power_cls.power_type == PowerType.DEBUFF` (a fixed class attribute) instead of C#'s sign-aware `canonicalPower.GetTypeForAmount(amount) != PowerType.Debuff` (ArtifactPower.cs:24; definition PowerModel.cs:460-471: `if (StackType==Counter && AllowNegative && amount<0) return Debuff;`). Strength/Dexterity are Counter + AllowNegative + Type=>Buff on both sides, so a negative-amount application is a Debuff by C#'s rule but bypasses the sim's Artifact branch entirely. REACHABILITY (dormant, corrected in fix pass 1): this gap is dormant in BOTH directions. (a) Player-side -- a player-held Artifact meeting an incoming negative-amount Strength/Dexterity steal -- is unreachable because NO player-side ArtifactPower source exists anywhere in the game. Exhaustive check: `grep -rl ArtifactPower --include=*.cs` over the whole decompiled game returns exactly 12 files -- PowerModel/AbstractModelSubtypes plumbing, ArtifactPower.cs itself, Mocks/MockArtifactMonster.cs, ONE card (Expose.cs:40-43, which only REMOVES Artifact from an enemy, never grants it), and 8 monsters (Aeonglass.cs:84, Chomper.cs:52, CubexConstruct.cs:91, MechaKnight.cs:76, PunchConstruct.cs:74, TheAdversaryMkOne.cs:32, TheAdversaryMkTwo.cs:36, TheAdversaryMkThree.cs:34) every one of which SELF-applies (`PowerCmd.Apply<ArtifactPower>(..., base.Creature, N, base.Creature, null)`). No relic, potion, event, or card grants ArtifactPower to a player, so the player-targeted steals at sts2_rl/monsters/glory/the_lost_and_forgotten.py:54,99 and sts2_rl/monsters/underdocks/lagavulin_matriarch.py:106-107 can never meet a player-held Artifact. (b) Enemy-side -- the player applying a negative-amount Buff to an Artifact-holding enemy -- needs a card that does so, and the only two in C# are Malaise.cs:39 and Resonance.cs:33, NEITHER of which is ported (grep confirms no sts2_rl/cards/*.py match). CONCRETE TRIGGER that would make this live: porting Malaise or Resonance (each applies negative StrengthPower to an enemy, and enemies genuinely do hold Artifact -- Mecha Knight, Cubex Construct, the Adversary line). G1 and G2 are therefore two faces of ONE dormant gap with the same named trigger. Pinned with an xfail exercising the enemy-side (Malaise/Resonance) direction: test/test_hook_order.py::TestPowerCmdOrder::test_artifact_blocks_negative_signed_debuff.

guards.what: G2: Same sign-aware gap in UnsettlingLamp's own doubling condition, plus an amount<=0 early bail; currently dormant
guards.issue: sts2_rl/relics/unsettling_lamp.py:44-53's modify_power_amount bails on `amount <= 0` and then checks the static `power_cls.power_type != PowerType.DEBUFF`, instead of C#'s `power.GetTypeForAmount(amount) != PowerType.Debuff` (UnsettlingLamp.cs:124), which classifies a NEGATIVE amount on an AllowNegative buff (e.g. Strength/Dexterity) as Debuff and would double it. C#'s Malaise.cs:40 and Resonance.cs:33 both apply negative StrengthPower to an enemy with applier=player, cardSource=this -- exactly the shape Lamp is meant to double. Neither card is ported in the sim yet (grep confirms no sts2_rl/cards/*.py match for either name), so this is dormant, but it would misfire (fail to ever double) the instant either card is ported, since the sim's amount<=0 guard rejects ANY negative-amount application before the sign-aware check would even matter.

guards.what: G3: C#'s three ordered phases (BeforePowerAmountChanged event / ModifyPowerAmountGiven chain / ModifyPowerAmountReceived predicate chain) collapsed into one registration-order-dependent chain; Artifact bypasses the hook-listener system entirely
guards.issue: hooks.py:170-183's modify_power_amount is a single flat chain over hook-registration order with no phase separation, unlike C#'s three separately-sequenced calls (PowerCmd.cs:120,125,127) that guarantee given-before-received regardless of listener registration order. Additionally, ArtifactPower is not a modify_power_amount listener at all in the sim -- it is hard-coded as a direct block in cmds.py:299-306, outside the hook loop entirely (see its own docstring, sts2_rl/powers.py:315-325: 'This power has no active hook methods; it is intercepted by PowerCmd.apply'). The two general modify_power_amount listeners that DO exist -- UnsettlingLamp (given-side, debuff-only) and RuinedHelmet (received-side, StrengthPower-buff-only, sts2_rl/relics/ruined_helmet.py:23-39) -- are domain-disjoint today (one only touches debuffs, the other only touches a specific positive-amount buff), so no live collision is demonstrated. But nothing in the sim's architecture would enforce correct given-before-received ordering for two future listeners whose domains DO overlap, the way C#'s fixed three-call sequence does by construction.

Hook.cs declares AfterModifyingPowerAmountGiven (Hook.cs:796-809) and AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived (Hook.cs:811-824), both of which the brief specifically flagged (2 of the 13 AfterModifying* variants Task 5's damage_pipeline audit found the sim implements only 1 of). The sim's hooks.py:170-183 modify_power_amount returns a bare aggregated int with no out-param modifiers list at all -- unlike its sibling modify_hp_lost/after_modify_hp_lost pair (hooks.py:126-154), which Task 5's re-audit found DOES carry this machinery (built for BufferPower). This is not merely a bookkeeping gap: ArtifactPower.AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived (ArtifactPower.cs:38-41) is the actual method that calls PowerCmd.Decrement(this) in C# -- the sim reimplements that specific effect inline in cmds.py:301-305, and RuinedHelmet.AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived (RuinedHelmet.cs:55-60), a SECOND real C# listener, likewise has its 'mark used' side effect folded directly into modify_power_amount in the sim (relics/ruined_helmet.py:37) instead of a separate after-hook. Framing corrected in fix pass 1: this is NOT dormant machinery with a single listener -- C# has two live listeners on AfterModifyingPowerAmountReceived today, and the sim hand-inlines BOTH. Each inline reimplementation is individually faithful in effect (verdict on steps 22/32 is about the missing dispatch, not about wrong Artifact/RuinedHelmet behavior), and no THIRD listener exists to be silently dropped -- but the correctness of both existing listeners currently rests on hand-inlining rather than on the mechanism, and the sim's modify_power_amount (hooks.py:170-183) returns a bare aggregated int with no out-param modifiers list at all, so a future listener needing the 'only react on the hit(s) where I actually changed something' pattern has nothing to hook into. AfterModifyingPowerAmountGiven (Hook.cs:796-809) is separately absent with no sim analogue at all.

guards.what: G5: No PowerInstanceType (Instanced / InstancedPerApplier) distinction in FindExistingInstanceForStacking
guards.issue: PowerCmd.cs:165-174's FindExistingInstanceForStacking dispatches on power.InstanceType (PowerModel.cs:144, default None); the sim's stacking check (cmds.py:308, `if power_cls.id in target.powers`) always behaves as None (single shared instance per power id per owner) with no instance_type concept anywhere in the sim. TWENTY-ONE C# powers declare an InstanceType override (counts corrected in fix pass 1 by re-running `grep "InstanceType" src/Core/Models/Powers/*.cs`: 21 hits, 19 Instanced + 2 InstancedPerApplier -- OblivionPower.cs:27 and StranglePower.cs:29). ELEVEN are ported in the sim: AutomationPower, HeistPower, PanachePower, RollingBoulderPower, SandpitPower, StranglePower (InstancedPerApplier, powers.py:2833-2869), SwipePower, TheBombPower, ThieveryPower, ToricToughnessPower, WitheringPresencePower. Of those eleven, only ToricToughnessPower and TheBombPower explicitly document the None-approximation and hand-roll a workaround bundling multiple logical instances inside one power's internal list (powers.py:1191-1200, 3748-3753); the other NINE do not acknowledge the distinction in their docstrings or implementation at all. The TEN unported ones are CoveredPower, FlankingPower, GuardedPower, KnockdownPower, MagicBombPower, MonologuePower, NightmarePower, OblivionPower, OrbitPower, TagTeamPower (each verified absent from sts2_rl/ by class-name grep) -- they will need the distinction considered when ported. No currently-demonstrated collision (only one copy of each is realistically active on a given owner in present content), but a second simultaneous instance on the same owner (e.g. two Thieving Hoppers' Swipe on the same player, or Strangle applied to one target by two different appliers) would silently merge via on_stack in the sim where C# tracks them as independent instances.

guards.what: N1: IsVisible is entirely absent from the sim's Power model; C#'s power.IsVisible gate (UnsettlingLamp.cs:93, ArtifactPower.cs:29-33) provably never varies
guards.rationale: A full grep of src/Core/Models/Powers/*.cs for `IsVisibleInternal` (the only way to override the default-true PowerModel.IsVisible, PowerModel.cs:150-167) returns zero matches anywhere in the entire C# codebase -- not just Ironclad-scope. IsVisible is therefore provably always true for every power in the current game, in both the Lamp's own latch gate and Artifact's own intercept gate. The sim's total omission of the concept produces no currently observable divergence, and cannot until new C# content introduces an invisible power (which would itself require a source-code change upstream, not just an unported-content gap) -- this is dead code in the source itself, not merely unported.

guards.what: N2: TemporaryStrengthPower/TemporaryDexterityPower's internal wrapped-power application omits applier in the sim instead of C#'s explicit HasDoubledTemporaryPowerSource double-dip guard
guards.rationale: C#'s TemporaryStrengthPower.BeforeApplied (TemporaryStrengthPower.cs:146-156) re-applies its InternallyAppliedPower (StrengthPower) via a full separate PowerCmd.Apply<T> call carrying the SAME applier/cardSource as the wrapper's own application, which would let UnsettlingLamp double both the wrapper (e.g. ManglePower, a Debuff) AND the internal StrengthPower independently (quadrupling) without UnsettlingLamp.HasDoubledTemporaryPowerSource (UnsettlingLamp.cs:164-167) explicitly detecting and skipping the second doubling. The sim's TemporaryStrengthPower/TemporaryDexterityPower counterparts (powers.py:840-870, 920-940) instead OMIT the applier parameter entirely on the internal StrengthPower/DexterityPower application (`PowerCmd.apply(hooks, owner, StrengthPower, self._sign * amount)`, no applier= kwarg) -- since UnsettlingLamp's own modify_power_amount requires `applier is self.player` to trigger at all, the applier-less internal call is naturally skipped, achieving the same 'double once, not twice' outcome by a different mechanism. VERIFIED BY EXECUTION in fix pass 1 (the earlier record rested on a hand-trace a reviewer could not re-derive). Sim run, throwaway script against the current worktree: with UnsettlingLamp active and the card bracket open, `PowerCmd.apply(hooks, enemy, ManglePower, 3, applier=player)` produces `{'strength': StrengthPower(-6), 'mangle': ManglePower(6)}` -- net -6 Strength, doubled exactly once. Control with no Lamp: `{'strength': StrengthPower(-3), 'mangle': ManglePower(3)}`. Real card play of the ported Mangle (StrengthLoss 10) with Lamp: `{'strength': StrengthPower(-20), 'mangle': ManglePower(20)}`; without Lamp: `-10`/`10`. Playing Mangle then Bash leaves Bash's Vulnerable at 2 (undoubled), so the Lamp's once-per-combat activation is spent exactly once. C# side, read line-by-line and matching: Hook.BeforePowerAmountChanged latches TriggeringCard=Mangle and adds ManglePower to DoubledPowers (UnsettlingLamp.cs:71-104; ManglePower.GetTypeForAmount(+3)=Debuff); ModifyPowerAmountGivenMultiplicative returns 2m for the wrapper because HasDoubledTemporaryPowerSource(ManglePower) is false (its InternallyAppliedPower is StrengthPower, not ManglePower), giving ManglePower(6); TemporaryStrengthPower.BeforeApplied (TemporaryStrengthPower.cs:145-156) then re-applies StrengthPower with Sign*6 = -6 carrying the same applier/cardSource, and on THAT call HasDoubledTemporaryPowerSource(StrengthPower) is true (UnsettlingLamp.cs:164-167), so the multiplicative returns 1m -- StrengthPower(-6), not -12. Both codebases therefore net -6 Strength (and -20 for the real 10-point Mangle). EQUIVALENCE HOLDS. Recorded as deliberate-divergence rather than faithful because the mechanisms genuinely differ (C# detects the double-dip explicitly; the sim avoids it by omitting `applier` so Lamp's `applier is self.player` gate fails) and a future power with a DIFFERENT double-dip shape -- e.g. one whose internal application legitimately needs an applier, or a Lamp-like relic that does not gate on applier -- could expose the difference.

guards.what: N3: Artifact's owner-scoping (target != base.Owner in C#, a hook-iteration self-filter) vs the sim's direct target.powers.get("artifact") lookup
guards.rationale: C#'s ArtifactPower.TryModifyPowerAmountReceived is discovered via IterateCombatHookListeners (iterating every hook-listening model in the whole combat) and self-filters with `if (target != base.Owner) return false` (ArtifactPower.cs:19-23) to only intercept when the power is being applied to Artifact's own owner. The sim's cmds.py:300 `target.powers.get("artifact")` directly looks up whether the TARGET (not some other creature) holds Artifact -- architecturally a special case instead of a hook-iteration self-filter, but semantically identical: both only ever have the target's own Artifact stack intercept a debuff aimed at that same target.

guards.what: N4: ModifyAmount's missing CanReceivePowers check (spec step 25) is a faithful absence, not a divergence
guards.rationale: C#'s ModifyAmount (PowerCmd.cs:215-271) itself only checks combatState==null, never CanReceivePowers, unlike Apply<T>/Apply(power,...) which check it twice (steps 2, 16). The sim's stacking branch (cmds.py:308-321) likewise has no CanReceivePowers-equivalent check -- both codebases omit it identically in the re-stacking path, so this is not a sim-vs-C# divergence at all, merely an asymmetry already present within the C# source between its own two power-application pipelines.
